look_here_first: LOOK HERE FIRST: Check for a persistent woody shrub with many short gray-green wedge-shaped leaves, commonly ending in three short rounded teeth. Confirm gray-brown woody stems and, when present, upright sprays of tiny heads. Three tips alone are not proof: compare the shrub habit and leaf proportions.

key_traits.label: Habit
key_traits.text: Aromatic, gray-haired, woody shrub typically 0.4–2 m tall, sometimes larger; substantial older trunks and branches with exfoliating gray bark; not rhizomatous.

key_traits.label: Leaves attachment
key_traits.text: Persistent small gray-green leaves on shoots, typically wedge-shaped, 0.5–3.5 cm long and narrow, commonly shallowly three-lobed at tip with rounded lobes; some leaves may be entire.

key_traits.label: Flower reproductive
key_traits.text: Tiny discoid heads in upright, branching panicle-like clusters; narrow involucres around 1.5–4 mm long, with woolly phyllaries; no showy rays.

key_traits.label: Fruit seed
key_traits.text: Small dry one-seeded cypselae around 1–2 mm; inspect under magnification.

key_traits.label: Stem bud
key_traits.text: Woody gray-brown branches, gray bark peeling in strips; gray-hairy vegetative growth.
